title: Incident containment + routing playbook discovery with Zenith Financials
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-25
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Ava (Redwood AE), Rohan (Redwood SE), Lina (Redwood CSM), Maya (Zenith Head Platform), Ethan (SRE), Priya (Security), Samir (Backend), Ally (Product)

Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect):
Zenith is evaluating Redwood for a mix of hosted and dedicated deployments. Primary concerns are incident containment, routing policies during region outages, partial degradation behavior (some endpoints remain live), SLA expectations for critical payment flows, and auditability for regulatory teams. They want a playbook: how Redwood would route traffic, fallback order, degraded mode behavior, and what visibility/metrics/logs they'd get. Next steps: share security pack and run a small smoke benchmark with sample traffic; meet again for a dedicated technical deep dive and an internal architecture alignment.

Topics:
- Multi-region routing and prioritization
- Canary vs instant failover policies
- Partial degradation and graceful response modes
- SLA numbers and financial exposure for missed SLOs
- Logging, audit trails, KMS and SSO/SCIM
- Benchmarks: p50/p95/p99 and cold start behavior

Transcript body:
[00:00] Ava (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick intro, I'm Ava, AE on the West, and with me is Rohan, our SE. Lina's here for ops follow up. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Maya (Zenith): Good, thanks. Quick note we have product and infra on, want to make sure we're aligned on what a partial outage looks like for you.
[00:20] Rohan (Redwood SE): Totally. I want to ask first about your critical paths — you mentioned payments are highest priority?
[00:27] Ally (Product): Yeah payments and account auth are top. Search / recommendations are secondary, okay to be degraded.
[00:33] Ethan (SRE): Right, so for payments we need sub 200ms tail for 95% ideally, and an SLA we can go to finance with. If a region goes down we need deterministic fallback.
[00:44] Ava: Understood. Boston vs us-west or multi-cloud? What's the target topology?
[00:50] Maya: We have prod in us-east and us-west, with a DR region in eu-west for compliance. We're exploring Redwood hosted for dev, and Dedicated or Private for prod depending on the guarantees.
[01:05] Priya (Security): Yeah security question up front — SOC2, encryption at rest, KMS integration, and audit logs. Also SSO: we use Okta with SAML and SCIM provisioning.
[01:18] Rohan: All supported. Quick caveat, auto transcriber's gonna butcher some acronyms, but yes SAML/Sesame, jk. We have KMS hooks and can bring your own key in Private. Audit logs are available per-request with token-level tracing.
[01:34] Samir (Backend): Walk us through routing — if us-east loses access to the model pool what happens? Do you fail to a smaller quantized model? Do requests queue?
[01:45] Rohan: Great question. We typically define a fallback chain in the routing policy: first try same-region full model, if capacity or region unreachable then route to cross-region identical model (same size) if latency budget allows, else route to a cheaper model variant in region (quantized or distilled) or finally to a cached response if prefix matches. You can tune per-route policies — latency budget, acceptable quality drop, and whether to return an error vs degraded response.
[02:12] Ethan: If we route to a cheaper model, do you surface that to the caller? We need the app to be able to tag responses that were degraded so downstream teams can reconcile.
[02:22] Rohan: Yes, we attach metadata headers and tokens, e.g., x-redwood-model, x-redwood-degraded: true, plus confidence scores if you enable quality telemetry. That metadata can also be forwarded to your logs.
[02:33] Maya: How about partial degradation — say only embedding service loses capacity, can you still serve generation?
[02:41] Rohan: Services are plumbed by route. You can split embeddings and generation into separate pools and set independent fallback chains. If embedding pool is degraded we can optionally return a best-effort embedding, mark it degraded, and route generation to models with local caching so downstream tasks still succeed.
[02:55] Ally: What's the behavior for streaming responses if region hops occur mid-request?
[03:01] Rohan: We try to avoid in-flight migrations. The runtime pins a request to a runner; if the runner fails mid-request we either retry on a compatible runner (if within latency budget) or return a truncated stream with an error chunk. We also support checkpointing tokens in some private setups to resume, but it's not common on hosted yet.
[03:22] Priya: For audit/compliance, can you provide immutable logs of request+response? We need retention 7 years for some data categories.
[03:31] Ava: We have long-term audit export options — logs can be exported to your S3/GCS with object immutability and retention policies. In Private deployments you can keep everything in your VPC with your KMS. Hosted has export and retention tiers per contract.
[03:47] Ethan: SLA — what do you guarantee for Dedicated and Hosted? Any credits for missed latency SLOs?
[03:54] Ava: Hosted API is our standard SLA for uptime; Dedicated comes with a higher SLA and financial credits tied to availability and end-to-end latency windows for committed capacity. Exact numbers are in the enterprise SLA packet — e.g., 99.9% for Dedicated. We can share the doc.
[04:09] Maya: We'd like to know assumed mean time to recovery on incidents. Also escalation paths.
[04:16] Lina (CSM): If you go Dedicated we provide a named CSM and platform on-call hook; for Hosted we have standard support and a priority escalation lane for enterprise. MTTR depends on root cause, but we have standard runbooks and an IR team.
[04:31] Samir: Can we see a playbook example? Like step A: region down -> re-route policy -> notify -> post-mortem steps.
[04:40] Rohan: Absolutely — we can share a runbook template. Quick sketch in-line: 1) Detect via healthchecks and region markers; 2) Auto-route traffic per policy; 3) Activate degraded endpoints flag; 4) Notify via webhooks and pager; 5) Kick off canary rollback if bad model behavior; 6) Post-incident audit with request traces.
[04:58] Ethan: About detection — do you integrate with our PagerDuty and existing SLOs?
[05:04] Rohan: Yes PagerDuty, Datadog, New Relic, and you can wire metrics into your SLOs. We emit p50/p95/p99 latencies, error rates, dropped tokens, queue length, cache hit ratios.
[05:16] Priya: Encryption: in-flight TLS ok, but for Private we need HSM-backed KMS key which we rotate. How do you manage key rotation and access logs?
[05:27] Ava: For Private we give KMS integration and support HSMs; key rotation can be automated with your KMS policies. Access logs for key usage are part of the audit trail.
[05:37] Ally: Any gotchas with VPC peering and egress costs if we route cross-region?
[05:43] Rohan: Egress is a factor. For cross-region failovers we can route to a region in the same cloud (lower egress) and set burst capacity or direct peering to reduce costs. We help model costs in the onboarding workbook.
[05:55] Maya: Competitor check — we've also talked to Anthropic and a few infra vendors. What makes Redwood's approach different for incident containment?
[06:04] Ava: Two pieces — runtime-level controls (continuous batching, pinned runners, KV caching) that reduce surface area for failures, plus a declarative routing/policy layer that lets you define quality/latency tradeoffs per route. Also we focus on observability that ties tokens to cost and quality.
[06:20] Ethan: Request: can you show an example routing policy DSL?
[06:25] Rohan: Quick demo in the follow-up doc. Example snippet: acceptLatencyMs: 200, fallbackChain: [same-size-same-region, same-size-cross-region, quantized-local], degradeMode: return-stub-or-error, notifyOnFallback: true.
[06:40] Maya: For the quantized fallback, is there a way to do A/B so we can measure quality delta?
[06:46] Rohan: Yes, you can do split traffic: canary percent to new model variant with quality metrics, or a shadow mode where degraded responses are logged but not used for production decisions.
[06:55] Samir: We need to avoid surprises for finance teams — if a fallback increases latency beyond our SLA, is there a contractual credit?
[07:03] Ava: The SLA table maps uptime and latency to credits for Dedicated. For Hosted we have published SLO targets and we can negotiate credits for committed usage with an enterprise agreement.
[07:12] Ally: Curious: how do you handle stateful context like KV cache when failing over regions? Do you lose the cache?
[07:19] Rohan: Cache is typically local to the runner/region. We do prefix-based KV cache export for cross-region warmups in Dedicated/private; otherwise losing cache is a tradeoff and that's why we recommend geo-warmup strategies for critical flows.
[07:31] Priya: Any regulatory restrictions on cross-border routing? We have EU PII that must stay in region for certain flows.
[07:38] Maya: Good point. We need per-route residency controls.
[07:41] Rohan: You can pin routes to regions and disallow cross-border fallback for those routes. For other routes you can allow cross-region. That's part of the policy DSL and console UI.
[07:52] Ethan: Let's talk about observability when fallbacks happen. How verbose are logs and what retention tiers?
[07:58] Rohan: By default we keep 90 days with full token-level traces for enterprise tiers; you can export to your retention store. Logged fields include request id, model id, runner id, latency, fallbackReason, degradedFlag, and side-channel quality metrics.
[08:12] Maya: Do you provide a simulation or dry-run so we can see how policies would behave under failover without impacting prod?
[08:18] Rohan: We have a policy simulator in the console and can run canary simulations against a synthetic traffic set to show routing decisions and expected latencies. We also do chaos-engineer style replay for Dedicated on request.
[08:30] Samir: Regarding cost, if we route cross-region or to larger runner, what controls prevent runaway spend?
[08:36] Lina: You can set budget caps and hard-fail thresholds in routing policies — e.g., only allow cross-region if estimated cost delta < X. We push alerts when thresholds approach.
[08:46] Ally: For the pilot we'd like a small Dedicated pool for payments and hosted for non-critical flows, is that something you see commonly?
[08:53] Ava: Yes, hybrid is common. Start with hosted for dev and non-critical, Dedicated for payments. Private is typical when they need strict residency and managed keys.
[09:02] Ethan: On benchmarks — we'll need p50/p95/p99 for our real payload sizes and QPS. Can you run a sample with our traffic pattern?
[09:09] Rohan: We can run a short benchmark. We'll need a sanitized sample payloads and target QPS. We can run against hosted or provision a temporary dedicated pool for more accurate numbers.
[09:18] Maya: Ok give us a timeline: if we decide to pilot next week, what are the steps?
[09:23] Ava: 1) Sign NDA if needed; 2) exchange security docs; 3) send sample payloads; 4) Redwood spins up sandbox dedicated or uses hosted with config; 5) run benchmarks and a technical deep dive; 6) iterate. Typical setup is 1-2 weeks for a small pilot.
[09:39] Priya: Can you send us the compliance pack and SOC2 attestation now?
[09:42] Ava: Yes will share.
[09:44] Maya: On the escalation path — who do we call if we see an outage?
[09:47] Lina: Enterprise customers get a named on-call line and a Slack channel. We'll share SLAs and contact info in the package.
[09:55] Samir: Action items for us: decide which flows are region-pinned vs allowed to cross-border; provide sample payloads; confirm budget cap.
[10:03] Ally: Also want the routing DSL example and playbook template.
[10:07] Ava: Great. Anything else?
[10:09] Ethan: Quick question — how do you handle rate-limiting during failovers to avoid thundering herd?
[10:15] Rohan: We have adaptive throttles and request queues with backpressure. You can configure burst windows and smoothing to prevent spikes.
[10:23] Maya: Perfect. Thanks everyone. We'll consolidate and pick dates for the deep technical session.

[End of transcript]

Notes about transcription quality: Some product names are slightly garbled by the auto transcript (e.g., K V cash for KV cache, SAML spelled Saml). Speaker labels were mostly accurate but two interjections were grouped as a single speaker in one chunk.
summary: Zenith Financials is exploring Redwood for a hybrid deployment: Hosted for non-critical flows and Dedicated (or Private) for payments and auth. Main concerns are deterministic routing/fallbacks during region outages, partial degradation behavior, SLA and credits, audit logs/KMS/SSO, and cost controls during failovers. Next steps include sharing security/compliance docs, running a sample benchmark with sanitized payloads, and a follow-up technical deep-dive to validate routing policies and playbook templates.
